anomalies.observed: The CAN transceivers’ GND1 and GND2 pins are both connected to GND, tying the two sides of each isolation barrier together.
anomalies.expected: For the specified isolated CAN interfaces, the logic-side and bus-side grounds should remain separate; tying both sides to GND defeats galvanic isolation.

evidence.quote: U11 shows pins GND1 and GND2 each connected to a GND symbol; U10 shows the same arrangement (sheet cm4-robot.kicad_sch, page 1).
“two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1) ... through an isolated CAN transceiver” (design specification, section 1).

anomalies.impact: The CAN signal paths may be internally isolated, but the shared ground connection bypasses that isolation, allowing ground differences and transients on the CAN side to couple into the logic side.

parsed.summary: The schematic connects both ground pins on each CAN isolation barrier to GND, defeating the galvanic isolation specified for the CAN interfaces.

Without an isolated supply, this doesn't seem genuinely galvanically isolated. I'll have to investigate if the ISO1050 component requires a separate supply on the bus side while sharing a ground. I’m wondering if the user expects me to identify a specific anomaly, but maybe there isn’t one? One interesting thing is the U36 e-stop /OE pin, which might be grounded.
